findings.title: Failed tool acquisition cleans up a monitoring ID it never acquired
findings.mechanism: self.tool is assigned by get_tool before use_tool_id succeeds. If another owner claims that ID at the claim boundary, use_tool_id raises ValueError; the except calls __exit__, which disables its events, unregisters callbacks and frees the foreign ID.
findings.reproduction: AST-extract the unchanged HOST_LAUNCH_DIAGNOSTIC string, bind actual SOURCE runtime_host, change only its fixed diagnostic path to a new private scratch file. Substitute sys.monitoring.use_tool_id with a deterministic claim-boundary injector: original_use(i,"safety-owned-foreign-canary"); original_use(i,name). Enter observer and catch ValueError. Read sys.monitoring.get_tool(i). It is None, not the canary. Restore the API and rescue only the owned canary if still present.
findings.limit: Deterministic same-process fault/claim-boundary control; not proof that a competing tool exists in the proposed isolated Host and not a universal adversarial race audit.
findings.minimal_fix: Track candidate versus successfully acquired tool ownership separately. Never unregister/disable/free on unsuccessful acquisition. Cleanup only the exact owned registration; retain uncertainty if ownership is lost. Add the failed-claim canary control without changing native observer registration or product methods.

findings.title: Monitoring teardown errors replace the primary exception and skip FD cleanup
findings.mechanism: set_events/register_callback/free_tool_id in __exit__ are outside the guarded cleanup. Any exception there escapes before saving INCOMPLETE or closing the owned FD; an active product exception is replaced.
findings.reproduction: On the actual extracted producer, replace only sys.monitoring.set_events so it calls the real API normally but raises synthetic OSError on disabling this observer ID. Raise a held ValueError instance inside with HostLaunchDiagnostic(). Observe the exception exiting the with; restore the API and invoke cleanup on this exact observer to rescue the test-owned tool/FD.
findings.limit: SOURCE tooling fault injection, no product runtime, no native launch; cancellation has the same unguarded code path but was not separately executed.
findings.minimal_fix: Make monitoring teardown failure-contained and attempt all exact-owned cleanup in finally. Preserve an already propagating primary exception/cancellation; mark evidence INCOMPLETE rather than replacing it or claiming STOPPED after tooling failure. With no primary, return a sanitized diagnostic failure or make the final strict gate refuse. Add one disable/unregister failure regression.
